findings.issue_text: [High/concurrency] Background legacy writes in dualwriter_mode3.go derive their context from the incoming request context (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)), which is canceled as soon as the HTTP handler returns, so the fire-and-forget legacy write races with request teardown and will frequently be aborted mid-flight, silently breaking mode 3's guarantee that legacy storage stays in sync; should use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (plus the timeout) or a detached context.

[High/data] The updateWrapper mechanism was removed, so d.Legacy.Update now receives the raw objInfo and independently recomputes the updated object from the legacy store's own (possibly different) old state; legacy and unified stores can now persist different contents, and objInfo.UpdatedObject is invoked twice per request (once per store), which is unsafe if the updater is non-idempotent or has side effects.

[Medium/api] Mode 3's externally observable contract changed from synchronous dual-write to asynchronous, best-effort legacy write without introducing a new mode number; any consumer that reads legacy storage immediately after a successful API write can now observe stale/missing data, and deployments already pinned to Mode3 get silently different semantics.

[Medium/bug] In the Create error path (dualwriter_mode3.go:47), storage failure is recorded with d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration, attributing storage errors/latency to the legacy store and corrupting the migration metrics.
[Medium/bug] In the Update error path (dualwriter_mode3.go:131), d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) is called on a unified-storage failure but should be recordStorageDuration.

[Medium/bug] In the DeleteCollection goroutine (dualwriter_mode3.go:168), the legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy) instead of recordLegacyDuration, so legacy deletions are counted as storage operations.

[Medium/bug] In the Delete success path (dualwriter_mode3.go:108), d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) passes the object name as the 'kind' label while every other call site uses options.Kind, producing inconsistent series and unbounded label cardinality (one series per object name).

[Medium/bug] Legacy write errors are completely swallowed: the goroutines capture the error only to flip a metric flag and never log it (previously each legacy failure was logged), so combined with the async design, permanent legacy/unified divergence is invisible to operators.

[Medium/concurrency] The legacy-write goroutines are untracked (no WaitGroup/queue/lifecycle management); Destroy() and process shutdown can race with in-flight legacy writes, risking use-after-close on the legacy store, and pending writes are silently lost on exit with no reconciliation mechanism.

[Medium/concurrency] Request-scoped mutable values are handed to background goroutines: obj (which legacy Create/Update may mutate, e.g. setting ResourceVersion/timestamps, while the same object may be aliased by the returned created/res being serialized into the API response) and the objInfo/validation closures (invoked after the request completed) — a data race / unsafe post-request use.

[Low/bug] In Delete (dualwriter_mode3.go:99), ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) uses the base logger instead of the just-built enriched log, so the name/kind/method values are dropped from the context logger used by the legacy-delete goroutine; all other methods correctly pass log.

[Medium/test_gap] legacyStoreMock and storageMock share a single mock.Mock, so expectations cannot distinguish which backend was invoked; concretely, the 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' case in TestMode3_Create sets no Storage.Create expectation and only passes because the legacy Create expectation intercepts the storage call on the shared mock.

[Medium/test_gap] No test verifies that legacy storage is actually written in mode 3: the async goroutines are never awaited and there are no call-count/AssertExpectations checks, so the core dual-write behavior (and the swapped metric calls and context-cancellation bug) is untested; the goroutines can also invoke the non-goroutine-safe testify mock after the subtest has finished, a flake/race risk under -race.

[Low/test_gap] TestMode3_Get creates a local p := prometheus.NewRegistry() while every other Mode3 test (and the Mode1 test, which was changed to rely on it) uses the shared package-level p; the inconsistent setup suggests duplicate metric registration on the shared registry is a live hazard — if NewDualWriter registers collectors per call, the shared-registry tests will fail or silently drop metrics.

[Low/bug] go.work.sum re-adds github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery v0.0.0-20240701135906-559738ce6ae1/go.mod, which is already present as an unchanged line, creating a duplicate entry and indicating the file was hand-edited rather than regenerated with go work sync/go mod tidy.

[Low/doc_defect] The doc comments in dualwriter_mode3.go still describe mode 3 as 'writing to LegacyStorage and Storage' with no mention that legacy writes are now asynchronous, time-boxed (10s), and best-effort with errors discarded; the material semantics change is undocumented for future maintainers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/concurrency] Background legacy writes in dualwriter_mode3.go derive their context from the incoming request context (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)), which is canceled as soon as the HTTP handler returns, so the fire-and-forget legacy write races with request teardown and will frequently be aborted mid-flight, silently breaking mode 3's guarantee that legacy storage stays in sync; should use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (plus the timeout) or a detached context.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Mode3 now performs legacy writes asynchronously via goroutines (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) and derives the goroutine context from the incoming ctx using context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...). Because this ctx is request-scoped (it’s also re-wrapped with klog.NewContext but not detached), it can be canceled by the upstream request teardown immediately after the main method returns, causing the background legacy operation to be canceled mid-flight. The code also ignores the legacy result/error (only records metrics), so this would silently reduce the chance that legacy storage stays in sync in mode 3. Detaching (e.g., context.WithoutCancel(ctx) + timeout) would address it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/data] The updateWrapper mechanism was removed, so d.Legacy.Update now receives the raw objInfo and independently recomputes the updated object from the legacy store's own (possibly different) old state; legacy and unified stores can now persist different contents, and objInfo.UpdatedObject is invoked twice per request (once per store), which is unsafe if the updater is non-idempotent or has side effects.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the previous logic that computed a single updated object once and then reused it for both stores via `updateWrapper` was removed. The new code calls `d.Storage.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` and then (in a goroutine) calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the same raw `objInfo` (no wrapper). This means each store will independently invoke `objInfo.UpdatedObject(...)` against its own "old" object/state, so the two writes can diverge if the stores differ or the updater is non-idempotent/has side effects. The diff directly shows the wrapper removal and passing `objInfo` unmodified into `d.Legacy.Update`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] Mode 3's externally observable contract changed from synchronous dual-write to asynchronous, best-effort legacy write without introducing a new mode number; any consumer that reads legacy storage immediately after a successful API write can now observe stale/missing data, and deployments already pinned to Mode3 get silently different semantics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Mode3 write paths changed from synchronous dual-write to asynchronous, best-effort legacy writes: Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection now perform the Unified Store operation and then spawn a `go func()` to call `d.Legacy.*` with a 10s timeout (`context.WithTimeoutCause`), returning to the caller immediately without waiting for legacy completion or propagating legacy errors. Previously these methods invoked `d.Legacy.*` inline (even if errors were often only logged). This is an externally observable semantics/backward-compatibility change for deployments pinned to Mode3 (legacy readers can see stale/missing data immediately after a successful API call), but it’s not verifiably a correctness defect without an explicit contract in the diff requiring synchronous legacy durability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] In the Create error path (dualwriter_mode3.go:47), storage failure is recorded with d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration, attributing storage errors/latency to the legacy store and corrupting the migration metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Create(), the storage call duration timer is started with startStorage := time.Now(), but on the error path after d.Storage.Create(...) fails, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage) instead of recording storage duration (it does call d.recordStorageDuration on the success path). This misattributes storage failures/latency to the legacy store and corrupts the metrics, exactly as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] In the Update error path (dualwriter_mode3.go:131), d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) is called on a unified-storage failure but should be recordStorageDuration.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, the Update method measures the unified store call with startStorage := time.Now() and then calls d.Storage.Update(...). In the error branch (storage failure), it records d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage), which mismatches both the timed operation (storage) and the intended metric name. It should record storage duration (recordStorageDuration) on a storage failure, not legacy duration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] In the DeleteCollection goroutine (dualwriter_mode3.go:168), the legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy) instead of recordLegacyDuration, so legacy deletions are counted as storage operations.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go within DeleteCollection, the async legacy write path calls `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)` but then records the duration using `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of a legacy-specific recorder (e.g., `recordLegacyDuration`). This will misattribute legacy DeleteCollection metrics as storage metrics, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] Legacy write errors are completely swallowed: the goroutines capture the error only to flip a metric flag and never log it (previously each legacy failure was logged), so combined with the async design, permanent legacy/unified divergence is invisible to operators.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes were changed to async goroutines for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection. Inside those goroutines the returned legacy error is only used to call recordLegacyDuration(err!=nil, ...) and is never logged (e.g., Create: _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Create(...); d.recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, ...)). Previously, legacy failures were explicitly logged (e.g., log.WithValues(...).Error(errLS, "could not delete from legacy store"); log.Error(errLeg, ...)). This is a diff-grounded observability regression, though not a direct functional correctness break since mode3 intentionally returns the unified-store result.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] The legacy-write goroutines are untracked (no WaitGroup/queue/lifecycle management); Destroy() and process shutdown can race with in-flight legacy writes, risking use-after-close on the legacy store, and pending writes are silently lost on exit with no reconciliation mechanism.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces untracked async legacy writes: Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection now spawn `go func() { ... d.Legacy.<op>(...) ... }()` without any WaitGroup/worker queue/cancellation or flush mechanism (e.g., `Create` and `Delete` in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`). That makes legacy writes best-effort and not lifecycle-managed. However, the specific claim about `Destroy()` causing use-after-close cannot be verified from the diff because `Destroy()`’s implementation is not shown, so an actual race/use-after-close is plausible but not provable from this patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] Request-scoped mutable values are handed to background goroutines: obj (which legacy Create/Update may mutate, e.g. setting ResourceVersion/timestamps, while the same object may be aliased by the returned created/res being serialized into the API response) and the objInfo/validation closures (invoked after the request completed) — a data race / unsafe post-request use.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the PR introduces background goroutines that reuse request-scoped inputs after the main call returns: Create() spawns a goroutine calling d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, createValidation, options); Update() spawns a goroutine calling d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, ..., options); Delete/DeleteCollection similarly pass validation funcs/options into goroutines. These values (runtime.Object `obj`, `objInfo`, and validation closures) are mutable and may be aliased with the object returned from Storage.* (common in k8s-style storage where the passed object is mutated and/or returned), so the goroutine can mutate/read concurrently with response serialization, creating a data race and “post-request” use of request-scoped state.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go the tests construct both backends with the same underlying testify mock: `m := &mock.Mock{}` then `ls := legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `us := storageMock{m, s}`. Because expectations are registered on `m` without a receiver distinction (e.g., `m.On("Create", ...)`), a Legacy expectation can satisfy a Storage call. Concretely in `TestMode3_Create` the case "error when creating object in the unified store fails" sets only a `Create` expectation via `setupLegacyFn` and no `setupStorageFn`, yet `DualWriterMode3.Create` calls `d.Storage.Create(...)` first; that storage call can match the legacy-registered `Create` expectation on the shared mock, making the test pass without actually proving which backend was invoked.

This inconsistency is real and could lead to duplicated collector registration or different metric behavior depending on how `NewDualWriter` uses the registry, but the diff does not prove a concrete defect because `NewDualWriter`’s registration behavior isn’t shown.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, the top-level comment still says “Mode 3 represents writing to LegacyStorage and Storage and reading from Storage.” However, the diff changes mode 3 write-path semantics: Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection now return based on Storage and perform Legacy writes asynchronously in a goroutine with context.WithTimeoutCause(..., 10s, ...) and no error propagation/logging (best-effort). That material behavior change is not reflected in the doc comments, which could mislead maintainers, but it is not a functional defect by itself.
